author: Slidebean
description:
How citizen recording is reshaping public accountability.

The rise of organized civilian recording often referred to as cop watching, is transforming surveillance from a one directional system into a shared public record.
As legal protections expand and platforms scale distribution, accountability increasingly emerges from visibility rather than authority alone.

This shift doesn’t eliminate surveillance, it redistributes it.

title: Surveillance is becoming a two way mirror

Just a few hundred miles separate the richest and poorest cities in the U.S. — but the gap feels far wider.

In this video, we travel from Country Life Acres, Missouri, one of the wealthiest micro-cities in the U.S., to Flint, Michigan, a city shaped by deindustrialization, state intervention, and the water crisis.
What connects them isn’t luck or hard work — it’s a system of legal loopholes, zoning rules, and governance structures that decide who gets to build walls… and who gets stuck paying the bill.

This is a story about wealth, power, exclusion — and the quiet rules that shape American cities.
